content.text:
Yes—with one important caveat.

Packslip is the right architectural answer because Atuin can declare both GNU and musl artifacts plus `requires.glibc_min = "2.39"` in signed release metadata. That keeps Atuin-specific policy out of mise’s Aqua backend. Atuin already publishes both builds and its installer performs exactly this fallback. [Discussion #12989](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12989), [Packslip host requirements](https://packslip.dev/docs/host-requirements/)

However, current Packslip semantics select the GNU artifact first and only then check its requirements. On glibc 2.38, mise would reject installation instead of retrying the musl artifact. The docs explicitly say requirements do not choose another build.

I think the clean solution is:

1. Extend mise’s Packslip backend so a confirmed incompatibility in the selected GNU artifact can trigger the existing static-musl fallback.
2. Preserve ambiguity safety: requirements must not decide between otherwise tied artifacts.
3. If the glibc check is unknown, retain the GNU artifact and warn.
4. Have Atuin publish Packslips declaring `glibc_min = "2.39"` on GNU builds.
5. Change [registry/atuin.toml](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/4081/mise/registry/atuin.toml) to prefer Packslip from the first release containing a manifest, with Aqua retained for older versions.

That solves this generically for every project shipping a newer-glibc build plus a static musl fallback—not just Atuin.
